correctness.rationale: With the zero-sum Euclidean normalization fixed, every centered dual 1-Lipschitz potential is the mean-zero projection of a point in the k-fold product of the six-vertex hexagon K_t. The strictly convex squared Euclidean norm has exact penalty \(k/2-t(1-t)E-W^2/(2k)\), with E split pairs and a signed W. For odd k, E=0 and E=1 yield precisely the two advertised penalties, and two explicit parameter-region inequalities strictly exclude \(E\ge2\); even k is optimized by balanced unsplit pairs. The counts follow by selecting parity-balanced signs and a single distinguished split pair. The contact-normal spans follow from the decomposition into k-1 pair-constant zero-sum and k within-pair antisymmetric directions; noncontact inequalities have strict slack. A standalone checker passed 23 exact rational configurations and 22 contact-rank checks. Finite cases corroborate, but the proof is analytic for every permitted real t.

The new complete Euclidean inball profile exhibits an interior parity-controlled symmetry-breaking threshold in the uniqueness of optimal centers, detects the precise changes in contacting facets, and measures the dimension of the entire optimal-center locus.
